identity.title: Adjudicate the operator-approved wreq transport exception

authorization.reference: After reviewing the measured WP-007 blockers and dependency alternatives, the Operator said: "ok lets go for your recommended path". This authorizes the recommended narrow BoringSSL-backed wreq and wreq-util exception for a bounded non-shipped dependency-adjudication integration, including an exact-pinned wreq 6.0.0-rc.29 candidate and stable wreq 5.3.0 control. It does not authorize product promotion, a general native-dependency exception, ambient proxy use, automatic redirect/cookie authority, transparent decompression, curl, curl-impersonate, Python, yt-dlp, or a browser runtime.

lifecycle.next_action: Await Operator direction before activating another work packet or authorizing any wreq product promotion.

DIFF_ATTACK_SURFACES: Contract and serialization boundary: configured emulation, semantic capability admission, strict dependency and fingerprint receipts, aggregate verdict fields, and live-network authorization.

Resource and lifecycle boundary: runtime-lane admission, request/read/total deadlines, body and report allocation, pool size, teardown inside and outside async contexts, and blocking dependency resolver behavior.

Integration and native supply-chain boundary: DNS and peer authority, proxy state, redirects, cookies, decompression, direct dependency attribution, native links, source markers, host variables, and supported-host limits.

Gate and oracle boundary: structural observation versus independent parity, stale checkpoints, forged PASS, removed blockers, report containment, collision handling, and zero-progress/product-promotion fields.
INDEPENDENT_CHECKS_RUN: Transport-security reviewer Halley independently traced operational profile admission, live-network bypasses, DNS/SSRF timing, structural fingerprint evidence, capability diagnostics, and stable-versus-RC proof; the pre-remediation verdict was FAIL.

Resource-architecture reviewer Poincare independently traced runtime locking, timeout and cancellation ownership, dependency resolver teardown, pool limits and partitioning, body/report allocation, and temp-root hygiene; the pre-remediation verdict was FAIL.

Oracle-integrity and native-supply-chain reviewer Anscombe independently traced FF-DEC-001 direct-edge attribution, all native-link packages, source/build overrides, stable/RC provenance, report identity, supported-host evidence, and product-promotion claims; the pre-remediation verdict was FAIL.

After remediation, the primary executed the 54-test transport matrix, 107-test xtask matrix, exact architecture gate, strict aggregate adjudication command, expected live-refusal command, and report mutation consumers.
COUNTERFACTUAL_CHECKS: Removing HTTP/2 from the release-candidate capability set changes the same operational boundary decision and is rejected.
Changing the strict aggregate verdict to PASS while residual blockers remain is rejected by a fresh deterministic reconstruction.
Adding a direct btls dependency with native=false is rejected because each direct edge reaching FF-DEC-001 must carry its own matching native decision.
Selecting zstd host discovery, removing packaged native source markers, or changing BoringSSL to a precompiled/FIPS surface is rejected by executable native-source policy tests.
BOUNDARY_PROBES: The public operational-profile method requests HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, body bounds, TLS and HTTP/2 fingerprint semantics, DNS provenance, SSRF policy, immutable pool partitioning, and cancellation before any network operation.
The explicitly authorized live API still returns typed DNS and SSRF blockers before dependency DNS or socket I/O; the CLI persists that refusal atomically.
An occupied runtime lane returns FF-WREQ-E-SATURATED immediately, and delayed loopback headers exercise the real wreq read-timeout path.
Aggregate and live reports are bounded while serializing, strictly reloaded, collision-safe, and canonically confined to repository build/reports.
NEGATIVE_PATH_CHECKS: Unsupported chrome-149-windows refuses without fallback; configured chrome-136 evidence remains observation-only and cannot upgrade HTTP/1.1 or parity status.
Ambient proxies, redirects, cookie storage, and transparent decompression remain disabled; oversized declared and unknown-length bodies fail at their bounded checks.
Nested runtime construction, runtime saturation, timeout, malformed wire receipts, outer/inner report mutations, oversized reports, report collisions, and escaped report paths fail closed.

Wrong native consumers, hidden native links, direct-edge misattribution, source overrides, feature drift, and unsupported-host mutations fail closed. No product promotion or production reachability is authorized.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.finding: A configured Chrome profile executed transport mechanics even though mandatory fingerprint, DNS/SSRF, pool, and cancellation semantics were blocked; public operational admission now requests the complete semantic set and refuses before I/O.
The library live API bypassed CLI opt-in and delegated DNS before Ferric SSRF authority; API-level authorization is now explicit and the live path refuses on DNS/SSRF before network I/O.
Mutex admission could wait outside the request deadline; the single execution lane now uses immediate typed saturation refusal.

Report encoding allocated an unbounded complete JSON vector before checking its size and tests used the external system temp root; bounded streaming serialization and repository-local test-runs now enforce the shared artifact policy.
Lexical build/reports validation did not prevent a junction or symlink escape; production writers now canonicalize both repository and report parent before atomic commit.
A consumer-level native decision could mask another direct dependency reaching the governed native graph; every direct edge now requires its own allowed matching native decision.

Native source validation covered only BoringSSL packages and a narrow override name; every allowed native link now has a source/feature policy and relevant source/toolchain override variables fail closed.

No strict aggregate command bound stable/RC identities, residual blockers, zero progress, and product-promotion denial; the aggregate producer and independent reconstruction now reject forged PASS or field drift.
The candidate policy cited an unreachable unsanitized stable checkpoint; it now cites reachable sanitized checkpoint 7dae6b6 and the aggregate comparison records both exact dependency surfaces.
Release-candidate blockers reused std-first explanations; wreq now emits candidate-specific fingerprint, DNS/SSRF, pool, cancellation, and generic diagnostics.

RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Independent Chrome TLS ClientHello and HTTP/2 wire parity is not established; configured profile and endpoint echo remain structural observation only.

Ferric-authoritative DNS provenance, pre-connect and peer-address SSRF enforcement, immutable pool partitioning, and wreq cancellation including blocking resolver teardown are not implemented, so operational and live execution remain blocked.
A dependency response chunk may transiently exist before Ferric rejects accumulated body growth beyond its bound.
Native build and supported-host evidence is limited to the exact Windows MSVC host and declared packaged sources/tool discovery; no cross-platform product build or staged runtime is proven.
